purpose: Reconcile cache correctness vs effectiveness claims.

cache_correctness.evidence: Phase 5 gate tests (12 passed): stale commit rejection, wrong-content rejection, wrong-config fingerprint rejection, corrupted/truncated JSON rejection, status-field corruption protection, reuse classification, lineage completeness.
invariants_proven: Same commit, edited file content → reusable=False (tree_digest mismatch)
Status field flip from fail to pass → detected and rejected

cache_effectiveness.trend: REGRESSED — hit rate worsened from <50% to 16%

root_cause_analysis.high_change_volume: 806 dirty files trigger full-pipeline execution on every check()
root_cause_analysis.low_reuse_opportunities: Each test scenario creates unique temp files → unique cache keys → cache misses
root_cause_analysis.fingerprint_sensitivity: Config/toolchain fingerprints change between runs (pytest version, environment)

cache_effectiveness.verdict: Cache CORRECTNESS is proven. Cache EFFECTIVENESS is poor but architecturally explainable: the pipeline correctly invalidates on every change, and with 806 dirty files there are few reuse opportunities. This is not a bug — it is correct behavior under high churn.

claim_reconciliation.phase_11_remediation_claim: Operational validation demonstrates cache reuse and invalidation
claim_reconciliation.honest_assessment: Phase 5 proves cache validity (correctness). Phase 11 proves the mechanism works (planning + dry-run). But cache hit rate remains at 16% because the environment has high change volume. Calling cache 'resolved' conflates correctness with effectiveness — these are distinct dimensions.
